description: Which posted patches carry a line of code: search the + and - lines of every patch posted to the lists (attached or pasted inline, every version) for an identifier, a line or a hunk, e.g. REGBUF_NO_CHANGE or `heap_page_prune_opt(Relation relation, Buffer buffer`. One entry per series (thread): first_version and latest_version that carry it (message_id, date, from, version, the patch files with download urls, the matching lines with their source path), how many messages carry it, and commit: the commit that landed it (sha, date), found through the commit's Discussion: link, or null. Words match from a word start and whitespace runs match any whitespace (pgindent between versions); several lines must all be changed lines of one patch file. Series are ordered by first appearance. complete=false (cut says why) when a common word hit the read cap or the budget ran out. At most 4 run at once; past that the call returns busy (retry). Hidden and taken-down mail is never returned. Different from search_patches, which reads [PATCH vN m/k] subjects. Read a version with get_attachment or the files' urls.

budget_ms.description: Time budget in ms (100-15000, default 10000). complete=false when it ran out.

case_sensitive.description: true (default) or false, a JSON boolean

inbox.description: One mailing list, e.g. pgsql-hackers. Default: every list.

query.description: Identifier, line or lines (a hunk) to find in the patches' changed lines. A leading + or - names the side of that line. A hunk takes at most 32 changed lines (repeated lines count once).

side.description: any (default): added or removed lines; added: lines the patch adds; removed: lines it removes

name: search_patch_lines
